Commentary.Commentary: The game set to begin. West Indies players stride out to the middle. Followed by Dimuth Karunaratne and Pathum Nissanka walk out to bat for Sri Lanka. Rahkeem Cornwall to start with the ball.

Right then, Sri Lanka will come out to bat with a lead of 156 runs. The West Indies need to pick some early wickets and make sure the batters don’t take the game away from them. With the current climate conditions, the bowlers will get some purchase off the pitch. A great session of play awaits do join us in short while.

Sri Lanka have been exceptional with both the blade and the ball. They put up a total of 386 in the first innings. Thanks to an impressive knock by their skipper, Dimuth Karunaratne, he was well supported by the batter from the other end. As they came out to bowl, it was their spinners bowled in tandem in the middle and caused a lot of problem to the opposition batters. Later, Ramesh Mendis came into the attack and picked up three wickets in quick succession to lead West Indies near the exit door. Praveen Jayawickrama was the pick of the bowlers with a four-wicket haul. Mendis bagged three wickets. While rest of the bowlers took a wicket each except Dushmantha Chameera.A job well done by the Sri Lankan bowlers.

West Indies tail order could not hang around for a longer period of time with just one wicket in hand. The top order could not get off to a solid start and it could’ve been gotten worse for the visitors but Cornwall, Mayers, Holder and Silva made sure to avoid the follow-on. Joshua Da Silva was the last remaining known batter in the middle at the start of Day 4. He could not handle the pressure alone, he tried to keep Gabriel off the strike for the most part of the over, but Gabriel could not survive an arm-ball of Jayawickrama.

Right. So just the 35 balls needed for Sri Lanka this morning to end the West Indian innings. Time is more of an important factor for them, as they need to dictate terms in the game, with time lost. Day 4 of the Test game, started off on a bad note with the rain gods smiling upon us. There was a delay to the start. And once the players came back on to resume play, Sri Lanka did not take much time to scalp the last wicket. Sri Lanka still have a lead of 156 runs under their sleeves.

OUT! LBW! Shannon Gabriel's resistance is over. A flighted ball from Praveen Jayawickrama, it was very full and angling on middle. Shannon Gabriel prods forward and looks to defend but is too late to get his bat down. The ball hits his boot. An appeal and up goes the finger. West Indies review it. UltraEdge shows no bat involved. Ball Tracker shows three reds and that is the end of West Indies' inning. They end at 230.
Review! Shannon Gabriel takes it upstairs for an lbw review. The on-field decision is out. The UltraEdge shows no bat is involved. The Ball Tracker shows three reds and Shannon Gabriel has to depart.
This one spins away sharply, flatter and outside off. Shannon Gabriel plants his front foot and leaves it alone.
An arm ball, angling on middle. Shannon Gabriel defends it.
Tosses it up, on middle. Shannon Gabriel makes a front foot defense.
Around off, pushed to covers.
Full and on middle. Joshua Da Silva blocks it back on the deck.
Slightly short and on off. Joshua Da Silva punches it to covers.
Tossed up on off. Joshua Da Silva prods and defends it on the off side.
Flatter, full and on off. Blocked out.
Very full and on middle. Joshua Da Silva lunges and blocks it out.
Full and on off. Joshua Da Silva defends it watchfully.
On the pads, Joshua Da Silva tucks it to square leg with soft hands to retain the strike.

NOT OUT! Joshua Da Silva survives. Looped up, around off. Joshua Da Silva prods forwards as he looks to defend it out but misses. The keeper collects the ball and was quick to clip the bails off. The umpire takes it upstairs to confirm. The replays show Joshua Da Silva had his back leg inside the crease.
Sri Lanka have reviewed for a caught behind and also for a stumping. UltraEdge confirms no bat there. The foot is grounded while the bails are dislodged and Joshua Da Silva survives.
On off, kept out.
Flatter, around off. Joshua Da Silva works it to mid off.
On off, blocked out.

What a delivery! Joshua Da Silva gets squared up. Loopy ball, around middle. The ball turns away. Joshua Da Silva looks to defend it out but gets beaten with the turn. Praveen Jayawickrama can't believe how the ball missed the off-stump here.
Lucky! Full and on off. Gabriel swings at it. The ball takes the inside edge, scoots past the stumps and goes towards fine leg. The batters take two before the fielder cuts it out.
Tossed up, full and on off. Gabriel defends it out watchfully.
Flatter, around off, Joshua Da Silva punches it towards cover for a single.
On off, Joshua Da Silva blocks it out.
Full, on the pads, Joshua Da Silva flicks it to square leg but goes against taking the single. Making sure the last man does not face many deliveries.
On off, blocked out watchfully.

EDGED BUT SAFE! Tossed up, around off. Shannon Gabriel looks to defend it out. The ball turns off the pitch and gets the outside edge off the blade. The ball goes to the right of the man at first slip and Gabriel survives.
Play and a miss! Looped up, around off. The ball turns away. Shannon Gabriel looks to defend it off the front foot but misses.
Flatter, on the pads. Joshua Da Silva hangs back and tucks it to square leg for a single.
Full, around middle and off. Joshua Da Silva drives it towards mid off.
Full and on off. Joshua Da Silva prods and defends it out watchfully.
Darted on the pads, a bit of turn this time. Joshua Da Silva goes back and defends it out with the full face of the bat.
Who will bowl from the other end? It is Praveen Jayawickrama.
Full toss, around leg. Shannon Gabriel clips it through mid on but does not get off the mark.
Flighted, full and on off. Shannon Gabriel prods and defends it out watchfully.
First runs of the day! Floated, around off. Joshua Da Silva pushes it to cover for a single.
Full and on middle. Joshua Da Silva defends it out to cover.
Flatter and around off. Joshua Da Silva punches it towards cover off the back foot.
Tossed up, outside off. The ball gets an extra bounce off the pitch. Joshua Da Silva leaves it alone.

We are all set to begin. The players of Sri Lanka stride out to the middle. Shannon Gabriel, the last man will join Joshua Da Silva in the middle. Lasith Embuldeniya to start with the ball. Also, Sri Lanka have taken the available new ball.

UPDATE 1011 Local Time (0441 GMT) - We have some good news for you! The covers are coming off and the play is set to begin at 1045 local time. We have lost 15 overs today but an updated schedule informs there are 91 overs scheduled to play if the rain doesn't play a part again.

UPDATE 0946 Local Time (0416 GMT) - We have officially passed the start time and it doesn't look good at the moment. The rain continues to be a spoilsport, not the start everyone was looking for. Stay tuned for further updates.

UPDATE 0924 Local Time (0354 GMT) - Well, not the ideal start to the day but the news coming from the center is that it is drizzling. It will be cloudy for most of the day. Expect a delay in the start.

Sri Lanka still have the advantage as they lead by 162 runs. They will look to stretch their lead by bundling out the visitors quickly. The forecast says rain will play its part as well but we hope that the rain gods stay away from the major part of the action. Fingers crossed. Stay tuned for other updates.

Day 3 saw rain play a part. The match was poised nicely but the rain gods had other plans. West Indies ended the day on a high note as at one stage they were 100/6 but Kyle Mayers, Holder and Cornwall played a key role and ended the day at  224/9. Most importantly they avoided the follow-on and will look for a big last partnership.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 4 of the first Test match between Sri Lanka and West Indies at Galle. Sri Lanka have an upper hand going into the play and they will look to take the last remaining wicket as soon as possible. For West Indies, they would hope to stretch the innings more and Joshua Da Silva will play a key role in that.
...Day 4, Session 1...

Right then, West Indies are still 162 runs behind and the wicket of Cornwall just before the rain delay means it's just a matter of time when they get bundled out but the visitors will look to extend their stay at the crease in the morning session as much as possible. This match is nicely poised, with the hosts still holding an advantage. However, if we have more rain and West Indies just keep holding on, they might escape with a draw and get some valuable points on the WTC table. Play will start at 0945 Local Time (0415 GMT) on 24th November. Do join us then. Till then, goodbye and take care!

Day 3 started off brightly with the West Indies lower order staging a remarkable comeback. The visitors went from hoping to avoid follow-on to adding 111 runs in the day with the loss of just three wickets. Sri Lanka spinners toiled hard early in the morning but did get the two set batsmen, Holder and Mayers out in quick succession. However, Rahkeem Cornwall and Joshua Da Silva did not let the hosts a get a grip on proceedings, with Cornwall hitting the spinners to all ends of the ground. In the second session, Cornwall did get out but then rain played spoilsport. Rain has been pouring all throughout the afternoon and after a couple of tries to get some play in, the umpires decided to call it a day. Things now get interesting, as we still have two more days to go and if the weather permits, this match can still end with a result. Sri Lanka will carry over their sizeable lead of 162 runs into Day 4 with just one more wicket to get.

UPDATE 1625 Local Time (1050 GMT) - We have the news everyone was expecting. Play has been called off for the day. Day 4 action will start a little early tomorrow morning at 0945 Local Time (0415 GMT).

UPDATE 1520 Local Time (0950 GMT) - Right then! The covers are off and the game is set to resume in about 10 minutes (1530 Local Time). Play can be extended till 1800 Local Time (1330 GMT) if possible. Oh, no! According to the latest reports from the ground, the rain is back. Just when play was about to resume, the rain Gods smile yet again and the waiting game will continue.

UPDATE 1500 Local Time ( 0930 GMT) - We have some good news, folks! It has stopped raining and the umpires are out in the middle having a chat with the groundstaff. The covers are coming off and the umpires will probably have an inspection anytime soon.
UPDATE 1426 Local Time (0856 GMT) - As expected, early Tea has been taken and there is still a steady drizzle at the ground. Stay tuned for further updates.

UPDATE 1353 Local Time (0823 GMT) - Just as we hoped that play would soon resume, the rain is back! Ground staff have to abort their mission to remove the covers and get the ones taken off, back on. Frustrating for players, the ground staff and all cricketing fans.

UPDATE 1343 Local Time (0813 GMT) - We have good news! The rain has stopped and the ground staff seem to be returning, to take the covers off. We will be back with more latest updates from the ground soon.

Shannon Gabriel is the last man in for West Indies. Just as he walks in, the play is halted. Rain showers have now started and before it gets heavy, the ground staff come out with the covers in a flash. The good thing is that there is still sunshine around the ground but for now we have a rain stoppage. Stay tuned as we bring you the latest updates from the ground.

OUT! TAKEN! Rahkeem Cornwall's fighting knock comes to an end and this is a much-needed breakthrough for the hosts! Lakmal comes back into the attack and does the job for his side straightaway! He hurls a well-directed bumper, around off. Cornwall looks to pull, gets cramped in the process and it goes off the top edge towards mid-wicket. Ramesh Mendis there runs behind, settles under it and takes a good catch. The Sri Lankans celebrate as the big man walks back.
Commentary.Howout: c Ramesh Mendis b Suranga Lakmal

Commentary.Commentary: Uppish but safe! Full ball, on the pads. Rahkeem Cornwall clips it past mid-wicket and collects a couple of runs.
Back of a length, around off. Rahkeem Cornwall blocks it off the back foot.
Wide! Lakmal bangs it into the deck, around middle. Rahkeem Cornwall ducks underneath and lets it through to the keeper. The umpire calls it a wide for the height!
Length ball, darted on the pads. Joshua Da Silva clips it to wide of deep mid-wicket for one.
Full ball, outside off. Joshua Da Silva presses forward and blocks it solidly.
Length ball, way outside off. Joshua Da Silva leaves it alone.
Suranga Lakmal (5-1-6-0) comes onto bowl for the first time today.
BEATEN! Flighted delivery, on a length, around off. Rahkeem Cornwall prods to drive but he misses and the ball goes past his blade.
Tossed up, on off. Rahkeem Cornwall defends it out.

An appeal for LBW but the umpire is not interested! Flatter ball, darted on the pads. Rahkeem Cornwall gets low to sweep but misses and gets hit on his pad. Lasith Embuldeniya puts in an appeal but the ball was going down leg.
Floated, around off. Rahkeem Cornwall presses forward to defend but it goes off the outer half past the silly point fielder.
Flatter ball, around off. Rahkeem Cornwall prods to block this one out.
Flighted delivery, around off. Rahkeem Cornwall is solid in his defence.
This is a length ball, angling in just that little bit from off. Joshua Da Silva defends it off the front foot.
Length ball, just outside off. Joshua Da Silva presses forward and blocks it to cover.
Length ball, middle on leg. Rahkeem Cornwall clips it off his pads towards deep square leg. The batters cross for a single.
Back of a length, outside off. Joshua Da Silva stays back, opens the face of his bat and guides it behind square on the off side for a run.
Good-length ball, around off. Joshua Da Silva defends it off the front foot.
Back of a length, outside off. Rahkeem Cornwall punches it past covers and takes a run.
Flatter ball, on off. Joshua Da Silva sits back and blocks it off the back foot.
Just a tad short, outside off. Joshua Da Silva stays back and cuts it to backward point.
Turn and bounce! Flighted delivery, outside off. Joshua Da Silva gets forward to defend but he misses as the ball spins past his outside edge.
Tossed up, outside off. Rahkeem Cornwall drives it to deep cover and takes a single.
Nicely tossed up, around off. Rahkeem Cornwall prods and defends it with soft hands. The ball takes the outside edge but doesn't carry to the slip fielder.
Flatter ball, outside off. Rahkeem Cornwall lets it be.
Who will bowl from the other end? It's going to be Lasith Embuldeniya.
This is a length ball, around off. Joshua Da Silva prods and pushes it gently towards mid on.
Short of a length delivery, around middle. Joshua Da Silva gets behind the line to block it from his crease.
Length ball, jagging back in from off. Joshua Da Silva blocks it off the front foot.
Chameera bangs it into the deck, around middle. Joshua Da Silva ducks underneath and lets it through to the keeper.
Length ball, angling in from middle. Joshua Da Silva prods to block it watchfully.
Intent from Cornwall, straightaway after Lunch! Good-length ball, around off. Cornwall looks to go downtown but it goes off the toe end just over mid on and the batters take a single.

We are back for the post Lunch session! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the Lankan players. Rahkeem Cornwall and Joshua Da Silva are back at the crease. Dushmantha Chameera has the ball in hand. There is rain further away from the stadium, so the groundsmen are keeping their equipment ready. Hope rain doesn't play spoilsport.
...Day 3, Session 2...

Right then, another riveting session of Test cricket has flown by where a total of 102 runs were scored from 33 overs and just 2 wickets fell. The game is still in the hands of the hosts but the visitors are making some significant progress with the bat. If they bat for an hour more, who knows what might happen later in this match. Join us soon for the second session as it promises to be mouth-watering.

Sri Lanka will be pleased in the end with the lead they still hold but it wasn't as easy as they expected this morning. It was all spin from the hosts as the pace bowlers just bowled two overs at the backend of the session. The surface was helping the spinners but they just couldn't find the right lengths consistently. The pair of Holder and Mayers attacked them early on but once they got rid of them, one would expect them to clean up the tail. This wasn't to be as Rahkeem Cornwall launched a counter attack which hurt the hosts and they don't have as big a lead. Sri Lanka will now be looking to come out guns blazing after Lunch and make sure they get rid of the remaining two wickets.

Resistance! Yes, it has been resistance of quite some quality, first from the overnight batters, Kyle Mayers and Jason Holder and then from Rahkeem Cornwall and Joshua Da Silva. The overnight batters not only survived the spinners but even countered with some classy shots. The pair added 50 runs this morning and 63 overall for the 7th wicket but then Mayers fell and Holder followed him to the pavilion soon after. This broke the Windies' backbone but Joshua Da Silva and Rahkeem Cornwall too batted well and made sure that the visitors avoided the follow on. They have already added 40 runs and the big man, Cornwall has taken a liking to the Lankan spinners as he hit some lusty blows.

Death by spin, is the term to be used for this Test match so far. 16 of the 18 wickets to fall so far have been taken by spinners and the visitors have really been mostly undone by the Lankan spinners. The first session on Day 3 has moved at a rate of knots and has been pretty even but in the end the visitors have just frustrated the hosts by extending their stay at the crease.
Flighted delivery, around off. Joshua Da Silva prods and blocks it solidly. That will be LUNCH on Day 3.
Floated, around off. Joshua Da Silva presses forward and blocks it.
Just a tad short, outside off. Joshua Da Silva sits back and cuts but the fielder at point dives to his left and stops the ball.
Flatter ball, around off. Joshua Da Silva pushes it to cover.
Flatter ball, on off. Joshua Da Silva defends it out.
FOUR! Cut away! Short ball, outside off. Joshua Da Silva stays back and cuts it past the point fielder. The fielder gives it a chase but the ball wins. 100 runs in the session for West Indies.
Back of a length, around off. Rahkeem Cornwall blocks it solidly off the back foot.
Wide! Chameera bends his back and bangs it into the deck, around off. Rahkeem Cornwall ducks underneath and the umpire calls it a wide.
Short of a length, outside off. Rahkeem Cornwall blocks it off the back foot.
Good-length ball, angling in from middle. Rahkeem Cornwall gets behind the line and is solid in his defence.
Chameera bangs it into the deck, outside off. Rahkeem Cornwall ducks underneath.
Back of a length, outside off. Rahkeem Cornwall leaves it alone.
Good-length ball, around off. Rahkeem Cornwall blocks it by getting behind the line of the ball.
Flighted delivery, around off. Joshua Da Silva defends it off the front foot.
Just a tad short, outside off. Joshua Da Silva cuts it straight to the backward point fielder, on the bounce.
Tossed up, outside off. Joshua Da Silva presses forward and blocks it out.
Floated, outside off. Joshua Da Silva looks to drive but the ball turns late and takes his outer half of the blade towards cover-point.
On a length, outside off. Joshua Da Silva prods and drives it to mid off.
Tossed up, outside off. Joshua Da Silva pushes it to cover.
A dot to end the over! Chameera fires in the yorker, around middle stump. Rahkeem Cornwall does really well to dig it out.
A 140 kph ball, on middle and slightly tailing in. Joshua Da Silva tucks it behind square on the leg side for a single.
A length ball, around off. Joshua Da Silva presses forward and keeps it out on the off side.
Nicely bowled, in the channel outside off and well left by Joshua Da Silva.
Full and straight, gently pushed to mid on.
Chammera starts with a length ball, on top of off. Joshua Da Silva plays it with soft hands on the off side.
Dushmantha Chameera (4-0-8-0) comes into the attack now.
Nicely tossed up, around off and stroked away to the cover region. Lasith Embuldeniya starts this spell with a maiden.
Flighted ball, on off and easily kept out by Cornwall.
Floated up, a bit fuller and on middle. Cornwall stays solid in defence.
Tossed up, around off and driven straight to covers.
Flatter delivery, on off and cut away off the back foot to cover-point.
Angled in at the leg stump. Cornwall strides out to defend.
On a length, around middle. Joshua Da Silva blocks it out watchfully.
Flighted delivery, around middle. Rahkeem Cornwall eases it to deep mid-wicket for one.
Flatter and quicker, turning in sharply. Rahkeem Cornwall does not offer any shot and gets hit high on his body.
FOUR! Cornwall is on the charge! Flatter ball, turning down leg. Cornwall stays back and whips it behind square on the leg side for another boundary.
FOUR! Nicely done! Fuller in length, just outside off. Rahkeem Cornwall drives it past the diving cover fielder and collects a boundary now.

SIX! Rahkeem Cornwall is making his intentions quite clear here! Tossed up, in the slot, around middle. Cornwall gets low and smacks it over deep mid-wicket for a biggie! West Indies bring up their 200!
Flatter ball, outside off, turning away. Rahkeem Cornwall sits back and pushes it to wide of cover-point and takes a run.
FOUR! TOP SHOT! Tossed up, outside off. Rahkeem Cornwall gets forward and carves it past cover to collect a boundary.
Flighted delivery, outside off. Rahkeem Cornwall presses forward to block this one.
Tossed up, on a length, around off. Rahkeem Cornwall prods to defend it.
Flatter ball, on off. Rahkeem Cornwall defends it out.
FOUR! WHACKED! Way too short, outside off. Cornwall rocks back and pulls it hard towards deep mid-wicket for a boundary.
Flatter ball, turning down leg. Joshua Da Silva leaves it alone.
Fuller in length, around off. Joshua Da Silva blocks it out.

Another chance goes begging! A very tough one though! Flatter ball, turning down leg. Joshua Da Silva looks to flick but gets the inner half of the blade and the ball goes quickly to the leg slip fielder who fails to gather it cleanly.
Fuller in length, on middle and leg. Joshua Da Silva blocks it out.
Floated, on a length, around leg. Rahkeem Cornwall tucks it to the leg side for a run.
Shouts of catch it, but it lands safely! Tossed up, around middle. Rahkeem Cornwall looks to flick but gets an inside edge onto his pad. The ball pops up but lands in front of the short leg fielder.
Nicely tossed up, on a length, around off. Joshua Da Silva blocks it off the front foot.
Fuller in length, outside off. Joshua Da Silva pushes it to cover.
Flatter ball, outside off, turning away. Joshua Da Silva stays back and punches it to extra cover.
Fuller one, on middle. Cornwall pushes it down to long on for one.
Beaten! Nicely flighted, outside off, inviting the drive. Rahkeem Cornwall goes for the cover drive but the ball grips and turns away sharply, going past the outside edge.
On a length, around off. Cornwall pushes it back to the bowler off the back foot.
Flatter and quicker, outside off. Joshua Da Silva is solid in his defence.
On a length, outside off. Joshua Da Silva blocks it watchfully off the front foot.
Flatter ball, on middle. Joshua Da Silva defends it off the front foot.
Fuller in length, around off. Joshua Da Silva blocks it out.
Flatter ball, turning down leg. Joshua Da Silva lets it be.
Fuller in length, on middle. Rahkeem Cornwall eases it down the ground and takes a single.

DROPPED! A tough one though! Tossed up, outside off, turning away late. Joshua Da Silva looks to heave it across the line but he only manages a thick outside edge. The ball goes to the left of the first slip fielder. Dhananjaya de Silva there dives but does not grab it cleanly.
Another ball, fuller in length, outside off. Joshua Da Silva keeps it out.
Loopy ball, on a length, outside off. Joshua Da Silva taps it towards backward point.
Tossed up, outside off. Joshua Da Silva presses forward and eases it to mid off.
Floated, on a length, around middle. Joshua Da Silva defends it to cover.
Flatter ball, on middle. Joshua Da Silva blocks it out.
Tossed up, outside off. Rahkeem Cornwall pushes it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Poor ball, and it gets the treatment! A half-tracker, around middle. Cornwall rocks back and pulls it along the ground behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
Tossed up, on a length, around off. Rahkeem Cornwall blocks it out.
Flatter ball, darted on the pads. Joshua Da Silva tucks it to the leg side and collects a run.
On a length, around middle. Joshua Da Silva defends it off the front foot.
Flatter ball, on middle. Joshua Da Silva skips down and blocks it.
BEATEN! Tossed up, outside off, going in with the angle. Cornwall looks to drive on the up but he misses as the ball sneaks through his bat.
Fuller in length, around off. Rahkeem Cornwall blocks it out.
On a length, outside off. Rahkeem Cornwall presses forward but leaves it in the end.
Just a tad short, outside off, turning away late. Rahkeem Cornwall looks to punch it but gets the outer half of the blade towards cover-point.
Floated, on a length, outside off. Cornwall pushes it to cover.
Tossed up, around off. Rahkeem Cornwall defends it off the front foot.
Flatter ball, darted on the pads. Joshua Da Silva defends it watchfully off the back foot.
Fuller in length, turning in sharply, around middle. Joshua Da Silva blocks it out.
A bit quicker and flatter, around midde. Joshua Da Silva tucks it to mid-wicket.
Flatter ball, on a length, around middle. Joshua Da Silva keeps it out.
Slightly shorter in length, on middle. Rahkeem Cornwall eases it to long on for a run.
Flatter ball, shorter in length, around middle. Cornwall tucks it to the leg side.
Floated, on a length, outside off. Rahkeem Cornwall drives hard but Ramesh Mendis does well to dive to his right to stop the ball. A single taken.
Tossed up, around middle. Rahkeem Cornwall prods to defend but he gets an inside edge onto his pad.
Rahkeem Cornwall is in at number 10.

OUT! TAKEN! Another stunning catch and this is a huge moment in this game as another set batter in Jason Holder walks back to the hut. The ploy to bring in Praveen Jayawickrama right after Drinks has worked for Sri Lanka as he strikes straightaway! Just a tad short, outside off, turning away late. Holder sits back and looks to cut but he gets a thick outside edge and the ball goes towards backward point. Dushmantha Chameera there dives to his right and completes a terrific catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Dushmantha Chameera b Praveen Jayawickrama

Commentary.Commentary: Nicely tossed up, outside off. Joshua Da Silva reaches out and drills it towards deep cover for one.
Just a tad short, outside off. Holder rocks back and cuts it to sweeper cover for a single.
Flatter ball, around middle. Jason Holder gets behind the line and blocks it.

DRINKS! West Indies' overnight batters started well but the wicket of Kyle Mayers just before Drinks will be a huge blow for them! Sri Lanka's spinners have been a tad inconsistent with their lines and lengths in this session so far and they will need to correct that and wrap things up quickly if they are to get a healthy first innings lead. Praveen Jayawickrama (12-4-25-2) comes back into the attack.
Tossed up, on middle and kept out by Joshua Da Silva.
Floated up, around middle. Joshua Da Silva presses forward and nudges it just past the short leg fielder.
On middle and this is worked through square leg for another one.
It's short again and down the leg side. Joshua Da Silva dabs it down towards short third man and gets the single. Good running.
Slightly shorter, on middle and leg. Holder flicks it off the back foot through mid-wicket and picks up a single.
SIX! Jason Holder decides that it's time to attack. Tossed up delivery by Mendis, Holder skips down the track and lifts it well over the wide long on fence for a biggie.
Ramesh Mendis (11-1-43-3) is back on.
Flatter delivery, attacking the stumps. Joshua Da Silva keeps it out.
Big turn but it's well outside the off stump. Joshua Da Silva isn't interested in playing at that one.
Well watched and well left by Joshua Da Silva. Around the off pole and turning away, Da Silva doesn't play at it.
On off and defended towards silly point.
Slightly fuller, on off and worked to cover-point.
Slowed up, on a length and around off. Da Silva plays it towards covers.
Dhananjaya de Silva comes around the wicket and spills it way down the leg side. No need to play at that.
Tossed up, Holder presses forward to defend.
On the stumps and blocked out by Holder.
On middle and leg, Joshua Da Silva nudges it towards mid-wicket and gets off the mark with a single.
Full and straight, pushed back to the bowler.
Joshua Da Silva walks out to bat.

OUT! TAKEN! What a ripper of a catch from the skipper, Dimuth Karunaratne! This is floated up by Dhananjaya de Silva around the off stump but it's not full enough. Kyle Mayers pushes at it with hard hands and that is his undoing. The ball pops up off the face of the ball, towards the right of the short cover fielder. Dimuth Karunaratne jumps to his right and the ball sticks in his right hand. This is a body blow for the Windies as Mayers falls short of his half-century. Sri Lankan players are delighted though.
Commentary.Howout: c Dimuth Karunaratne b Dhananjaya de Silva

Commentary.Commentary: Safe! First false stroke of the day from Jason Holder but he survives. Floated up, around off and inviting the batter to drive. Holder leans in to cover drive but gets an outside edge which loops up and falls well short of the backward point fielder.
On off and defended off the front foot this time by Holder.
A touch short and wide, played off the back foot to cover.
Just around the off stump and well left by Jason Holder.

We are ready for play! The Sri Lankan players are out on the field and so are the umpires. The overnight batters for West Indies, Jason Holder and Kyle Mayers take guard. Lasith Embuldeniya to start proceedings with the ball on Day 3.

Lasith Embuldeniya is down for a quick chat. He says that they want to get Windies out as soon as possible and they will think about follow on later. Adds ghat they wanted to score 400 but are happy with what they got. Tells that there is turn and bounce in this pitch and it will turn more as the game progresses. Says that he keeps things very simple and looks to turn the ball. Tells that he enjoys playing Test cricket and says that right from school cricket he has been playing longer format.

PITCH REPORT - Farvez Maharoof is pitchside. Aamer Sohail joins him and assesses that the pitch is turning and there's bounce on offer as well, making it even more difficult for the batters. He adds that there is a way to counter this and that is to stay positive and use their feet.

West Indies bowled well on Day 2 and managed to bowl out the hosts under 400. They did get off to a good start with the bat as well when their openers Brathwaite and Blackwood were able to see off the new ball. But once the spinners came on, they found it hard to cope with the turn and bounce and perished. Wickets kept tumbling as there was no respite from the Lankan spinners and the momentum shifted completely in Sri Lanka's favour. However, Kyle Mayers has come out with positive intent at no.7 and the visitors would hope that he goes on to get a big one for them. Jason Holder also has a great opportunity to show his worth with the bat and he would be keen to put on a show when his team needs him the most. We are in for an intriguing day of Test cricket so do not go anywhere as the action on Day 3 will begin shortly.

Sri Lanka put up a decent first innings score but their pacers failed to make early inroads and the Windies openers managed to go into the Tea break unscathed. However, once the spinners got into their act, Sri Lanka never looked back and picked up wickets at regular intervals. Ramesh Mendis was introduced late in the day but he made an immediate impression and grabbed 3 wickets which sent the visitors on the back foot. Embuldeniya and Jayawickrama also bowled well and kept the batters in check. Fair to say, it was a day which was dominated by Sri Lanka who find themselves in the driver's seat now!

Hello and a very warm welcome to Day 3 of the first Test between Sri Lanka and West Indies. The game has moved at the rate of knots in the latter half of Day 2 and the visitors are in a spot of bother at 113/6, courtesy of some fine bowling by the Lankan spinners. The pitch has started to turn square and the Windies have a mountain to climb as they are trailing hy 273 runs with only 4 wickets in hand. They do bat deep but the overnight batters have their task cut out and must take Windies to safer shores. Having said that, rain is predicted to play spoilsport on Day 3 but we hope that the rain gods stay away and we get to see another scintillating day of Test cricket.
...Day 3, Session 1...

Right then! That is all we have from this day. Day 3 is usually considered the moving day of a Test match and West Indies would surely hope that Day 3 moves in their favour. But that seems very difficult as the pitch is offering more and more help to the spinners. The first job for West Indies is to make sure that they avoid the follow on. Do join us on 23rd November at 10 am Local (4:30 am GMT) for the third day's action. Till then, goodbye and take care!

It was a topsy-turvy day for West Indies. At first, they seemed helpless with the ball but staged a superb comeback, led by their spinners, Roston Chase and Jomel Warrican. The visitors managed to restrict the hosts to a total below what was expected at one time, thanks to a five-wicket haul from Roston Chase. West Indies had a decent start with the bat as both Kraigg Brathwaite and Jermaine Blackwood saw the new ball through. It was when the spinners bowled in tandem that the Windies batters looked vulnerable. Apart from skipper Brathwaite, no one else put up much of a fight. Wickets kept on tumbling and the visitors find themselves reeling on 113 for 6 at the end of the second day. They still need 74 runs to avoid the follow on and it's going to be a tough ask for them on Day 3.

Sri Lanka had a set platform from Day 1 but as the second day progressed, they kept on losing their advantage with the bat. Only Dinesh Chandimal looked comfortable out in the middle as the hosts lost seven wickets inside two sessions and ended up putting 386 runs on the board when at one stage they looked to be on course for a score beyond 450. With the ball also they did not have the best of starts but as soon as they picked up the first wicket, their spinners got a grip on the match. Lasith Embuldeniya and Praveen Jayawickrama bowled well in tandem but after a while, the visitors got quite comfortable at the crease. Then Ramesh Mendis was brought in and he picked up 3 wickets in a flash, putting the Lankans on top of proceedings at the end of the second day.

What a riveting day of cricket we've had on Day 2! A total of 13 wickets fell in the day as the momentum kept on swinging either side and the contest between bat and ball was one to witness. In the end, the hosts will be the happier of the sides going into the third day as they take a huge lead of 273 runs into the next day, with West Indies only having four wickets remaining.

FOUR! Top shot to finish the day! Fuller ball, on off. Mayers gets to the ball and drives it nicely. Two fielders chase it. One of them dives but the ball wins the race. That ends what has been a fantastic session for Sri Lanka. STUMPS ON DAY 2!

Meanwhile, in Dhaka, a thrilling finish to the last T20I between Bangladesh and Pakistan. The visitors were in control of the chase and found themselves needing 8 in the last over with 8 wickets in hand. They lost 3 wickets but also scored 10 runs. Really dramatic finish. Mahmudullah took 3 wickets in that final over, he was on a hat-trick too but did not get it just like Mendis missed out on his hat-trick here. A thrilling finish to the T20I series!

Tossed up, around off. Nkrumah Bonner blocks it off the front foot.
Flatter ball, outside off. Nkrumah Bonner cuts it to cover-point.
Nkrumah Bonner is in at number 3.

OUT! LBW! Lasith Embuldeniya finally gets the breakthrough for Sri Lanka which they badly needed! He serves a loopy ball, around leg, turning away a bit. Jermaine Blackwood looks to tuck it to the leg side but he misses and gets rapped in front. Embuldeniya puts in an appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Blackwood reviews it straight away but the Ball Tracker shows three reds and he is a goner! West Indies also lose a review!

Jermaine Blackwood has straightaway taken the review for the LBW decision. UltraEdge shows that there's clear daylight between bat and pad. Ball Tracker shows that the ball was going on to crash into the leg stump. The onfield decision of OUT stays and West Indies lose a review as well.
Flatter and quicker, outside off. Kraigg Brathwaite sits back and lets it through to the keeper.
Another ball, fuller in length, outside off. Kraigg Brathwaite defends it out.
On a length, around off. Kraigg Brathwaite comes forward and blocks it.
Tossed up, outside off. Kraigg Brathwaite drives hard but finds the cover fielder.
Flatter ball, on a length, around middle. Kraigg Brathwaite skips down and eases it to mid on for a run.
Flighted ball, around off. Kraigg Brathwaite defends this one out.
Flatter ball, on a length, around off. Jermaine Blackwood blocks it solidly off the front foot.
Lovely delivery! Tossed up, around off, turning away sharply. Kraigg Brathwaite looks to defend but it goes off the outer half behind square on the off side. A single taken!
Flatter ball, around off. Kraigg Brathwaite prods and defends it off the front foot.
On a length, around off. Kraigg Brathwaite blocks it out.
Loopy ball, around middle and leg. Kraigg Brathwaite tucks it to the leg side.
Tossed up, around leg. Jermaine Blackwood turns it to wide of mid-wicket for a single.
On a length, just outside off. Kraigg Brathwaite prods to block this one out.
Just a tad short, outside off. Kraigg Brathwaite stays back and punches it to cover.
Nicely tossed up, around off. Kraigg Brathwaite drives hard but straight to mid off.
Floated, outside off. Kraigg Brathwaite defends it off the front foot.
Flatter ball, darted on the pads. Jermaine Blackwood tucks it to the leg side for one.
Tosses it up on off. Jermaine Blackwood pushes it back to the bowler.

Beaten! Nicely flighted, around off and just as Brathwaite looks to stride out and defend, the ball turns away sharply leaving him bamboozled. Lasith Embuldeniya has bowled these rippers but has often followed them with average deliveries, allowing the batters to pick up boundaries.
FOUR! Short and wide, Kraigg Brathwaite punishes it. Brathwaite rocks back and cuts it through cover-point and picks up a boundary.
Floated up, on middle. Brathwaite strides out to block it.
A touch shorter, around off and punched off the back foot towards extra cover.
Nicely bowled! Just outside off and the ball grips a bit. Brathwaite makes a watchful leave.
Flatter delivery, around middle. Brathwaite defends it off the back foot.
Round-arm ball, down leg. Jermaine Blackwood looks to flick but he misses.
Floated, down leg. Kraigg Brathwaite clips it behind square on the leg side for a run.
Loopy ball, around leg, turning away late. Kraigg Brathwaite looks to block but he gets deceived by the turn and gets an underedge behind the keeper.
Loopy ball, on leg. Kraigg Brathwaite pushes it back to the bowler.
Tossed up on middle. Kraigg Brathwaite drives it towards mid off.
Tossed up, on middle. Jermaine Blackwood eases it past the bowler and takes a single.
Praveen Jayawickrama is brought back into the attack.
Fuller ball, on off. Blocked back to the bowler.
Another solid defence by Kraigg Brathwaite.
Nicely tossed up, on off. Kraigg Brathwaite blocks it with ease.
Flatter ball, on off. Pushed to covers.
Tossed up, on the pads. Worked to mid on.
Sharp turn! Tossed up, on off. Kraigg Brathwaite plays in the line of the ball and looks to defend. But the ball spins away and goes past the outside edge.
Length ball, around off. Jermaine Blackwood hangs back and punches it to mid on.
Short again, outside off. Left alone and a wide has been called as the bowler exceeded the short ball limit.
Short of a length, around off. Jermaine Blackwood blocks it towards mid off this time.
On a length, around off. Jermaine Blackwood opens the face of the bat and plays it towards point.
Chameera bends his back and digs a short one, outside off. Jermaine Blackwood sways away from it.
Back of a length, around off. Pushed to covers with ease.
Back of a length, on off. Pushed back towards the bowler by Jermaine Blackwood.
Quicker and flatter, just outside off. Kraigg Brathwaite is aware of the off pole and leaves it.
Loopy ball, on off. Blocked out with ease this time.
RIPPER! Nicely tossed up, on off. Kraigg Brathwaite is drawn forward to block it. The ball turns sharply and goes past the outside edge.
Arm ball, on off. Kraigg Brathwaite runs it past backward point for one.
Loopy ball, on off. Blocked out.
FOUR! Poor ball and punished! Short ball, wide outside off.  Kraigg Brathwaite rocks back and cuts it hard past cover for a boundary.
Lasith Embuldeniya (3-1-14-0) comes back to bowl.
Chameera goes back to the short ball and Blackwood leaves it again.
Fuller again, on off. Jermaine Blackwood leans into it and blocks it. Chameera sticks his left hand out and gathers the ball.
Short ball, on off. Jermaine Blackwood sways away from the line of the ball.
Drifting down the leg side. Kraigg Brathwaite works it to fine leg for an easy single.
Fuller ball, on off. Pushed back to the bowler with soft hands.
Back of a length, on off. Jermaine Blackwood clips it past mid-wicket for a single.
Dushmantha Chameera (2-0-5-0) is back into the attack.
Length ball, right on the off pole. Kraigg Brathwaite presses forward and blocks it with soft hands.
Length ball, outside off. Left alone with ease.
Another short one and Kraigg Brathwaite ducks under this too.
Shorter ball, on off. Kraigg Brathwaite sits under it. The keeper dives to his left and collects it.
Fuller ball, lands on off and comes in with the angle. KB blocks it from the crease.
Length ball, on the pads. Worked past square leg for a single now.
Fired straight on the stumps. Kraigg Brathwaite offers the full face of the bat and blocks it.
Loopy ball, wider outside off. Left alone this time.
Well bowled and well left! Quicker and just outside off. KB thinks of blocking it but leaves it at the last moment.
Loopy ball, on middle. Kraigg Brathwaite gets forward to block it.
Tossed up, wide outside off. Left alone.
FOUR! Slapped! Shorter ball, outside off. Kraigg Brathwaite slaps it hard. The man at point dives over it and it runs to the fence.
Fuller ball, outside off. Kraigg Brathwaite leans into it and guides it past point. The fielder dives to his left and stops the ball. Still, the batters get a single.
Lakmal bowls it full, on off. A solid defence is offered by Kraigg Brathwaite.
On a length, wide enough for Kraigg Brathwaite to leave it with ease.
Back of a length, quite wide outside off. KB does not chase this one.
Fired on the pads. Kraigg Brathwaite taps it to mid-wicket.
Fuller ball, outside off. Kraigg Brathwaite leans into it and taps it to covers.
Suranga Lakmal (3-1-4-0) comes to bowl.
Another one outside off and left alone. An entertaining first over after Tea.
Loopy ball, wide outside off. Left alone.
SIX! Top shot! Tossed up, on off. Jermaine Blackwood heaves it straight down the ground for a maximum.

Beaten! Tossed up, just outside off. Blackwood looks to block but the ball turns sharply and goes past the bat. Chandimal gathers it and goes up in appeal but there is no bat on that. Just some vicious turn.
FOUR! Quality stroke! Darted on the pads by Lasith Embuldeniya. Jermaine Blackwood gets low and sweeps it hard to the square leg fence.
Tossed up, on off. Bit of turn on it. Blackwood looks to defend but gets the inside edge on the pads.
We are back for the last session on Day 2! The players stride out to the middle. Kraigg Brathwaite and Jermaine Blackwood take the crease. Lasith Embuldeniya to start the final session.
... Day 2, Session 3 ...

Sri Lanka have started well with the ball but they would be kicking themselves as they did not opt for a review when Jermaine Blackwood was trapped in front by Dushmantha Chameera. The spinners were introduced early and they troubled the Windies' opening batters right from the word go. Dimuth Karunaratne would hope that his spinners get some early breakthroughs post the Tea interval and put the visitors on the back foot. Another intriguing session of Test cricket awaits us which begins shortly!

West Indies have managed to go into the Tea break unscathed and that would ease some nerves in their dressing room. However, Jermaine Blackwood would consider himself very lucky as he was given a life by Sri Lanka when they decided to go against taking a review. Kraig Brathwaite looked good in the middle and he too got a life on the last ball before Tea when he reviewed his LBW decision. The ball has started to turn sharply and Windies have a steep task ahead of them.

NOT OUT! Kraigg Brathwaite survives on the final ball before tea! Tossed up, on middle and this one just slides on with the arm. Brathwaite looks to put out a stride and defend but misses and gets hit on the pads. Praveen Jayawickrama appeals and the umpire eventually raises his finger. Brathwaite reviews and Ball tracking confirms that the ball was sliding down the leg side. The umpire changes his decision and also signals for the Tea break. What a gripping session it has been!
Review time! Kraigg Brathwaite has opted for a review after being adjudged LBW by the umpire. The Sri Lankans are celebrating as they look really confident.
A touch shorter, on off. Brathwaite defends it off the back foot.
Tossed up, on off and Blackwood strides out looking to defend. The ball takes the outside edge and goes past first slip. They get a single.
That was a peach of a delivery! Nicely flighted, around the off stump. The ball grips and turns away sharply, leaving the batter bamboozled.
Floated up, on middle and Blackwood stays solid in defense.
Tossed up, around off and Blackwood defends it back to the bowler.
Praveen Jayawickrama comes to bowl now.
On middle again and kept out on the leg side.
Slowed up, on middle and watchfully defended out by Brathwaite.
Beautifully flighted, on middle and drawing the batter forward. Brathwaite blocks it out.
Tossed up, around off and kept out on the off side.
Poor second delivery from Lasith Embuldeniya. Full toss, on middle and Brathwaite misses out as he hits it straight into the wrist of the fielder at short leg.
Spin straightaway for Lasith Embuldeniya. Looped up, on middle and the ball grip and turns away sharply. Brathwaite plays it with soft hands but edges it just past the fielder at first slip.
Lasith Embuldeniya comes to bowl.
On top of off and kept out by Blackwood.
Lakmal goes fuller, on off and looking to bring the ball back in. Blackwood defends it off the front foot.
Back of a length, on off and pushing the batter on the back foot. Jermaine Blackwood remains solid in defense.
Full and straight, Blackwood punches it straight to mid on.
On middle and this is pushed towards mid-wicket.
A touch short and wide, Blackwood hangs back and cuts it through cover-point for a brace.
Length again, on middle and kept out on the off side.
Back of a length, around off and Brathwaite blocks it out.
Another spicy short ball. Brathwaite does well to duck under it.

LEG BYE! Oh, that looked really close! A length ball, angled in at middle and leg. Blackwood looks to flick but gets squared up and gets rapped on the pads. The hosts appeal but the umpire remains unmoved. The ball rolls towards backward point and they get a leg bye. The review isn't taken and maybe Sri Lanka just missed a trick here.
Well directed short ball from Dushmantha Chameera. Around off stump and at 142 kph. Blackwood sways away from the ball and hangs out his bat as well but misses the ball.
Good-length ball, outside off. Brathwaite hangs back and eases it to wide of cover-point for a single.
On a length, just outside off. Blackwood shoulders arms.
Lakmal pitches it up and bowls it outside off. Blackwood makes an assured leave.
Good-length ball, on off and this is punched towards the cover region.
Almost an action replay of the previous delivery. This time just the line was outside off.
Slightly shorter, around middle. Blackwood defends it off the back foot.
Blackwood is off the mark too! A length ball, angled in on middle and leg. Blackwood tucks it through mid-wicket and comes back for the second with ease.
FOUR! Width on offer and the Windies skipper gets off the mark in style. Short and wide, Brathwaite slaps it through backward point and picks up a boundary.
Back of a length, around middle and Brathwaite just manages to keep it out.
Full, around off and at 143 kph. Brathwaite punches it nicely but the fielder at short cover makes a really good diving stop.
Good-length ball, outside off and tapped straight to cover-point.
Chameera hits the length hard, around off. Brathwaite hops and taps it back onto the deck.
LEG BYE! Chameera starts off with a length ball, on the pads. Blackwood looks to flick but gets it off the pads towards short fine leg. They get a leg bye and West Indies are underway.
Who will bowl from the other end? Dushmantha Chameera it is.
A maiden to start proceedings! Around off and Brathwaite plays it with soft hands towards cover.
Right on the money from Lakmal. Again it's a probing line, around off and Brathwaite manages to keep it out on the off side.
In that channel outside off and Brathwaite just watchfully leaves it alone.
Length again, on off and defended back to the bowler by Brathwaite.
A slight bit of shape away from the right-hander. Around the off stump and moving away, Brathwaite let's it through to the keeper.
Lakmal starts off with a length ball on the pads. Kraigg Brathwaite tucks it towards mid-wicket from the middle of the bat.
